title: Root Makefile -- non-blocking review follow-up from PR #97
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #97 (dev-makefile-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: `make dev`'s fail-fast fix relies on bash's `wait -n <pids...>` with an explicit pid list, which needs bash >= 5.1 (this repo's devcontainer ships 5.3.9, confirmed fine). The new `SHELL := bash` line resolves `bash` by searching `PATH` (GNU Make's documented behavior for a non-absolute `SHELL` value), not a pinned/absolute path -- so outside the documented devcontainer workflow (e.g. a contributor running `make dev` directly on macOS, which ships an ancient bash 3.2.57 as `/bin/bash` by default for licensing reasons and lacks `wait -n` entirely), the recipe would fail with a bash syntax/option error rather than the old hang, and with a less obvious message than the venv/npm setup errors the other targets already print. Not blocking: the project's documented and supported workflow is the devcontainer (`.devcontainer/post-create.sh` guarantees bash 5.x), and `make backend` already gates on devcontainer-style setup with an explicit error message when things are missing, so this is consistent with existing conventions, not a regression. Worth considering if `make dev` is ever expected to run reliably outside the devcontainer: either document the bash >= 5.1 requirement in README's Quick Start alongside the devcontainer callout, or add a cheap version guard in the recipe with a clearer error than the raw bash syntax error.

Found by a `code-review` pass on PR #97 (independently re-verified before filing): `docs/tasks/done/dev-makefile-followups.json`'s `decisions[1]` rationale overstates what `wait -n`'s captured `status` actually carries -- it says `make dev`'s own exit code 'reflects whichever sub-target failed', but GNU Make's own process always exits with status 2 on any recipe/target failure regardless of the failing command's real exit code (verified directly: a target whose recipe does `exit 7` still yields `echo $?` -> 2, both in a scratch Makefile and this repo's own `backend` target). Since `bpid`/`fpid` are sub-`make` invocations (`$(MAKE) backend`/`$(MAKE) frontend`), a failure on either side surfaces to `wait -n` as that same code-2, not a value that distinguishes which side failed or carries the underlying command's real exit code -- only signal-caused termination (130/143/etc.) would differ. The actual runtime behavior (fail-fast, correct teardown, non-zero exit) is unaffected and correct; this is a documentation-accuracy issue in the decision's rationale text, not a code bug. Worth a follow-up edit to that `decisions` entry (or a short addendum) correcting the claim so a future reader doesn't rely on `make dev`'s exit code to infer which sub-target failed.

Found by the same `code-review` pass on PR #97: the 11-line bare-SIGINT-limitation comment above the `dev` recipe is written as individual `@#...` recipe lines (each starting a fresh recipe line prefixed with `@#`) rather than as a plain `#` Makefile comment above the `dev:` target -- inconsistent with the adjacent `SHELL := bash` rationale a few lines earlier in the same file, which correctly uses a plain `#` comment (zero runtime cost). Because GNU Make spawns one shell invocation per recipe line (confirmed via `make -d`: one 'Live child' per `@#` line), every `make dev` invocation currently forks ~11 extra no-op shell processes solely to carry comment text. Runtime cost is negligible (each fork is on the order of a millisecond, and `make dev` is an interactively-invoked dev tool, not a hot path), so non-blocking, but it's avoidable overhead and a style inconsistency within the same file -- moving the comment above the `dev:` target line (as a plain `#...` block, same as the `SHELL := bash` comment) would fix both.

decisions.decision: Documented the bash >= 5.1 requirement for `make dev`'s `wait -n` usage in two places: a short addition to README.md's 'Quick start (Makefile)' section (right after the existing devcontainer-dependency paragraph), and a tightened version of the existing Makefile comment above `SHELL := bash` that now states the version number explicitly and cross-references the README. Did not add a runtime version guard to the recipe.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item offered a choice ('either document ... or add a cheap version guard'); documenting is lower-risk and matches the project's existing devcontainer-first convention (`make backend` already just prints a clear error rather than gating with a version check, and the project's documented/supported workflow is the devcontainer, where the requirement is already satisfied). A runtime guard would need its own bash-version-parsing logic that itself has to work under whatever `bash` is found on `PATH` (including bash 3.2, which lacks features a naive guard might reach for), adding complexity to fix an already-non-blocking edge case. Put the primary documentation in README's Quick Start (as the checklist item suggested) rather than only in the Makefile comment, since README is what a contributor reads before ever opening the Makefile; kept and tightened the Makefile-local comment too since someone debugging a `wait -n` failure in the recipe itself is more likely to be looking at the Makefile than scrolling back to README.

decisions.decision: Corrected `docs/tasks/done/dev-makefile-followups.json`'s `decisions[1]` by editing the overstated sentence in place (removing the 'reflects whichever sub-target failed' claim) and appending a dated correction note to the same `decision` field explaining what `$$status` actually carries (GNU Make's own code-2 for a sub-`make` recipe failure on either side, indistinguishable between `backend`/`frontend`; only signal-caused codes like 130/143 differ), rather than rewriting the entry's history silently or adding a wholly separate new decisions entry.
decisions.rationale: Editing in place with a visible, dated correction note preserves the original entry's context (still explains why `wait -n` + re-kill + re-wait was chosen, which is unaffected) while making the inaccurate claim impossible to miss for a future reader of that same entry -- an easy thing to overlook if the fix were logged only in this task's own `decisions` array on a different file. Rejected silently rewriting the sentence with no trace of the correction: CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule is about making judgment calls discoverable, and silently editing history without any marker would hide that a claim was ever wrong, which is exactly the kind of thing a later reader (or another agent citing that entry) should be able to see. Rejected adding a brand new `decisions` entry on the *done* task file instead of editing the existing one: the correction is squarely about that one sentence in `decisions[1]`, and appending it as a note right next to the sentence it corrects is more discoverable than a same-array entry with no explicit back-reference other than an index number that could drift.

decisions.decision: Moved the 11-line bare-SIGINT-limitation comment from individual `@#`-prefixed recipe lines (inside the `dev:` recipe body) to a plain `#`-prefixed Makefile comment block directly above the `dev:` target line, reworded slightly (from first person about 'this recipe' to 'the recipe' since the comment is no longer physically inside the recipe) but otherwise preserving the original content verbatim.
decisions.rationale: This is exactly what the checklist item asked for and matches the style already used for the `SHELL := bash` rationale a few lines above in the same file -- zero runtime cost (no per-line shell fork) versus the previous ~11 extra no-op `sh -c '#...'` forks per `make dev` invocation. Verified `make -n dev` and `make help` produce identical output before and after the move, and re-ran the fail-fast (backend/.venv moved aside: exits ~instantly, non-zero status, no leftover processes, ports free) and clean-shutdown (SIGTERM to a healthy `make dev`: exit 143, no orphans, ports free) scenarios from `dev-makefile-followups`'s own decisions against the moved comment to confirm the recipe's actual behavior is unchanged.
